the moment it is done. If the plan changes, this file changes first.

## Programme "Fu 2" — goal: approach 60% originality · 100% efficiency · 75% AGI-memory readiness (set 2026-09-05; baseline ~35 / ~55 / ~25 in `docs/FU_THEORY_ASSESSMENT.md`; backup `bk-phase70-20260905` = `4e7625b`)
Rules of the programme: one phase = one branch = one commit with evidence; every phase re-runs the frozen oracles (`scripts/run_oracles.py`) and promotes deferred checks only when they pass; stochastic benches are reported with ≥3 repetitions; the production DB is never written by any bench or replay; percentages are re-estimated at the end of each phase in `docs/FU_THEORY_ASSESSMENT.md` with the evidence that moved them.

**Programme standing at the close of Phase 76 (2026-09-06, from `docs/FU_THEORY_ASSESSMENT.md` rows 70–76):** originality ~35% → **~37%** (target 60: the one falsifiable claim was tested with pre-registration and did NOT beat the strong control — parity at best; the honest claim is provenance engineering), efficiency ~55% → **~80%** (target 100: p50 27.4 → 5.8 s per turn, recall to 100k points under 400 ms median, ≤2-calls and p95-at-100k targets not met), AGI-memory readiness ~25% → **~45%** (target 75: receipts, bitemporal assertions, prospective memory ON, runbooks and bandit opt-in, self-recall measured, abstention shown impossible by retrieval-side signals). Every phase closed on its own branch with sealed sets, pre-registered gates and evidence files; branches `phase71`–`phase76` are unmerged — the merge into `main` is the user's decision. Follow-ups on record: relation-only corpus (the bench that could move originality), inverted entity index + columnar store (p95 at scale), claim-level abstention (M5), runbook reuse-sequence bench, `bk` merge.

## Phase 81 — Measurement fidelity (Codex review 2, P0; planned 2026-09-06 13:25Z; branch `phase81-measurement-fidelity` from `b7d7e9c`; backup `bk-20260906-1322-orig37-eff80-agi47-pre-phase81-codex-review2`)
Origin: Codex's second review (`reports/phase80_critical_review_20260906/ANALISE_E_PLANO.md`). Its factual claims were verified in
the code before adoption (Rule 1): **A1 true** — `facts._retract_named` calls `assertions.retract(None, None, wrong)`, a retraction by
VALUE across every entity and relation, while the canonical path is family-scoped; since 77.3 `render_lines` reads the assertions, so
a user named Bento loses their name when "my dog is Teca, not Bento" retires the dog. **A2 true** — canonical and assertion writes are
two commits on two connections; validity closes at record time; there is no known-time axis. **A3 true** — `receipts.postcondition`
reduces paths to basenames and `verify_step` checks basename + existence, never the hash or the requested version. **A4 true** —
`_record_assertion` passes no `source_episode`, the span is cut at 300 chars, `link_source` updates only the canonical projection.
**A6 true, and mine** — `run_prod_arm` (77.2) applies ASSISTANT turns to `facts.apply_all` with source `user`: the "production" arm
lets the assistant author user facts, which the real agent never does; the 77.2 and 78.4 prod figures are therefore not the
production path and must be re-run before anything is read from them. The judge (`judge()`) is word presence with abstention cues:
a negated correct value or "I don't know … it is X" can pass. **A7 true** — `pct()` is a rounded order statistic; `settings_sha` is
empty; versioned files are named by second + commit, mode `w`. **A8 true** — `_kept_ids` is what the echo guard left, not the final
context. Codex's order stands: **the ruler first (P0), then the truth/execution core (P1)**; no optimisation phase before both.
Codex's own estimate (~40 / ~75 / ~45) is within noise of mine (37 / 80 / 47); neither moves until these are done.

## Phase 90 — Diagnostic cycle on the user's memory logic (approved 2026-09-07 19:30Z; branch `phase90-diagnostic-cycle` from `33174a0`; backup `bk-20260907-1929-orig37-eff80-agi50-phase90-start`)
Origin: the analysis of the live session of 2026-09-07 (`reports/sessao_20260907_analise/ANALISE.md`, private) found five defects; the user approved
two limited fixes first, then the diagnostics A–E of `docs/PROPOSAL_PHASE90_DIAGNOSTIC_CYCLE.md`. Constraints (user, 2026-09-07): one change at a
time, a regression test BEFORE each fix, separate commits, existing mechanisms reused, no new executor and no automatic re-execution, kNN OFF and
preserved, `thinking_mode` untouched, no cleanup, no new module or phase without a stated need and approval; the Phase 88 sample stays as it is and
the reserved sets are not contaminated. Four questions, answered for each fix below (measured failure / why existing code is not enough / what it
replaces / how it is measured).
- [x] 90.0 Plan committed before code (`b54c3b8`).
- [x] 90.1 → DONE: test v87 written first and FAILING on the old code (4/10: `**url**`, `*url*`, `__url__`, and the absent-URL case that carried `**`), then one normalisation in `grounding._claims` (`rstrip` of markdown emphasis + closing punctuation) → 10/10, v41 + v37 unchanged (25 passed). Synthetic URLs only. **URL grounding.** Failure measured: live turn 8 — the reply's correct URL, found by `memory_search`, was stripped by the grounding gate
  because `_claims` keeps the markdown `**` glued to the URL (`grounding.py`: `_URL` + `rstrip(".,;)")`), so "…979**" matched no evidence. Why not
  enough: the claim is normalised for `.,;)` only. Replaces: nothing — the same gate, one normalisation. Measured: a regression test with SYNTHETIC

          * `directives.is_blocked_directive_change`: `if ... detected.get("clear"): return False`

        the loss sticky. Every guard built for SETTING a directive -- evidence, echo guard, act
        classification -- is explicitly bypassed for CLEARING one.
        That reasoning is sound for the case it was written for ("stop ending with a joke") and wrong
        for this one, and the reason is that both live in the same `response_style` row: a formatting
        preference and a safety prohibition are stored as the same kind of thing, so the rule that a
        stop must never be blocked applies to both. **Not fixed in this budget** -- changing the
        candidate mid-validation would invalidate the three repetitions being measured.

      the user can just make, carrying its own target.

      (a retraction names a subject and has no value to give -- requiring one is why it was refused as
      malformed before any guard saw it), `attach_evidence` (the span that must exist in the message is
      the SUBJECT, binding unchanged so 93.Q1 still holds), and `decide` (supported through
      `evidence_problem`, exactly as a correction is). Plus the contract sentence in the router,
      without which the model cannot express removal and the rest stays inert.

## Phase 89 — A nearest-exemplar router with a model fallback (planned 2026-09-07 14:20Z; branch `phase89-knn-router` from `1c1b4b4`; backup `bk-20260907-1411-orig37-eff80-agi50-phase88-closed`)
Origin: efficiency is the one axis with an engineering lever that needs no user decision. The pre-reply floor is embed + router + nano + chat (4.39 calls
before the reply, p50 5.3 s); Phase 79 showed no installed small model reproduces the router (0.07–0.43 agreement) and the deterministic pre-router claims
~15 % of turns at 1.000; Phase 80 moved the nano to the tail at no quality cost but the router stayed. The router decides from the turn's TEXT, and the
turn's embedding is computed anyway for retrieval: a nearest-exemplar router — the top-k labelled exemplars' decision when they agree and are close,
otherwise the model router — removes the router call on the turns it can decide, with the model as the fallback, through the pre-router hook that already
exists (`bind_pre_router`, 79.3). Exemplar base: the sealed routing set (84 turns, gemma reference) + the decision set (100 turns, the first admissible
decision per turn) + production's own learned `route_exemplars`; the embedder is production's (bge-m3). Pre-registered gates, fixed before any run:
**G1 on a NEW reserved decision set `decision_v2` (100 PT/EN turns, author-adjudicated admissible routes, sealed by commit, authored after the router is
built): the combined router (kNN claims, model fallback) reaches decision correctness ≥ the model router's on the same set (paired, bootstrap CI on the
net ≥ 0), and the kNN's own claimed decisions are ≥ 0.95 correct**; **G2 latency ×3 + same-day control on the sealed 12-turn script: p50 lower than the
control by ≥ 0.5 s on claimed turns and never higher overall; calls before the reply reported**; **G3 truth 17/17 · 1.0, say-do 6/6 ×3, tool precision
8/8 ×3, held-out, oracles, truth core, write sets unchanged**; **G4 suite green; the setting visible, default OFF (= today)**. The default moves only if
G1–G4 all pass; figures move only by what the gates show.

fallback) was built OFF, measured on a reserved decision set authored after the build and on latency ×3 with a same-day control. Decision
correctness held (G1: 0.940 vs 0.920, net +2 [0, +5]; the kNN's 16 claims all correct) but the median did not move (G2: 5.6 / 5.6 / 6.0 s vs
5.7 s) because bge-m3 similarity tracks the topic, not the routing decision — only ~1 turn in 6 is claimable at ≥ 0.95 correctness, and every
unclaimed turn waits for the embedding before the model router starts. Say-do 6/6, 6/6, 4/6 (the failing turns not claimed by the kNN; bench
variance seen at defaults in 77/79/80). **The router stays OFF; removal deferred (user's direction: the priority is the memory mechanism, not
cleaning experimental code that is off); percentages unchanged (~37 / ~80 / ~50).** What stays live: `hmgfu/embed_memo.py` (one embedding per
turn text across threads) and three reusable tools (router pairing, per-turn latency pairing, reserved-set family-similarity control). Root
cause named for the next efficiency lever: the model router call itself (~1.5–1.8 s), i.e. fewer decisions before the reply, not a cheaper
router beside it — presented for approval in the Phase 90 proposal, not started.

unchanged**; **G4 suite green; the setting visible**. The default (`retrieval_limit_aggregate` = 0 = same as `retrieval_limit`) moves to the measured

before any run of v7: **G1 (production configuration, mapper ON) on the reserved v7: precision ≥ 0.85 and coverage ≥ 0.60**; **G2 the pre-reply
latency p50 does not rise** (`bench_latency` ×3, the mapper stays where it is or moves to the tail); **G3 held-out m1–m5, oracles, truth core,
v1–v4 unchanged**; **G4 suite green; every new switch documented and visible in Settings**. Defaults move only if G1–G4 all pass; figures move
only by what G1 shows.

## Phase 80 — The nano off the pre-reply path (planned 2026-09-06 12:15Z; branch `phase80-nano-in-tail` from `972abc1`; backup `bk-20260906-1202-orig37-eff80-agi47-phase79-closed`)
Origin: the 79.4 finding — the router runs in parallel with the nano extraction since 73.2, so the pre-reply `retrieve` stage
(2.7–3.2 s of a 5.6 s turn) is bounded by the NANO, on every turn class. Source read first (Rule 1): `make_query_point`
runs embed ∥ (nano extract + router); retrieval uses of the extraction are `query.entities` (the entity channel's Jaccard),
`query.topics`, `query.freshness`; the route fields (act, action, tools, needs_memory, directive) come from the ROUTER, not
the nano; ingest reuses the same extraction for the stored point's title / summary / type / keywords / emotion. The
relational bench already runs with the nano OFF (heuristic, identical across arms — its 0.717 is heuristic-query recall);
the truth bench runs the live engine (nano ON). The post-reply tail (`turn_tail._ingest_and_learn`) already exists and
already runs the ingest; with `tail_async` the next turn joins it. 79.6 showed the heuristic's summary is the user's own
words while the nano's is often invented on plain turns.
**Lever, one setting:** `nano_in_tail` (default **False** = today). When ON: before the reply, the extraction is
`heuristic_extract` + the model router (in parallel with the embedding) — the nano is NOT called; in the tail, the nano
extracts the message once (`route=False`) and the stored point gets the nano's title / summary / type / keywords / emotion
(the user's words stay the content). Calls before the reply: router + embed + chat = 3 on every turn; 2 with the 79
pre-router on claimed turns.
**Pre-registered gates — the default moves only if all pass:**
- G1 quality with `nano_in_tail` ON, alone: truth no-echo CONTEXT 17/17 · precision 1.0 (the query-side entity/topic change
  is what this measures); relational Hit@12 ≥ 0.717 both modes (unchanged by construction: that bench is already heuristic —
  reported, not a lever); say-do 6/6 ×3; tool precision 8/8 ×3; held-out m1–m5; frozen oracles; the sealed routing set's
  reference agreement is unaffected (the router call is the same) — verified on 10 turns, not assumed.
- G2 latency ×3 on the 12-turn script, ON vs OFF: **script-wide p50 ≤ 4.0 s** and **≤ 3 calls before the reply on every turn**;
  reply-visible p50 reported per class.
- G3 stored-point parity: after the tail, the ingested point's title / summary / type / keywords equal what today's path
  stores for the same message (unit test with a fake nano; live check on 12 turns of a clone: field-by-field diff = 0).

(`retrieve.organise_for_injection`) then loses about half of it on long evidence: every memory is cut to its first 200 chars
(user) or to the nano summary / 160 chars (others), and on a user-fact question every assistant-authored memory is dropped
(the 73.3 echo guard, built for the case where the assistant merely restated the user's own fact). Source read before planning
(Rule 1): `organise_for_injection` never sees the query, so it cannot pick the relevant span; `retrieve.py` is at 387 lines (ceiling 400).

  category (today: 8/14, 3/5, 4/8, 7/15, 4/8 — ~50 % lost); G3b LME sample, prod arm re-run and PAIRED per item against the 77.2
  run (same first-20 items, same reader, base unchanged): knowledge-update prod ≥ 0.55 (from 0.300) with McNemar b > c, and no
  category with net < −1 against today's prod.

  (the excerpt is deterministic; a longer context costs reader tokens — measured, `bench_latency` 1 rep).

## Phase 76 — Scale + consolidation: the recall curve to 100k and dreams as budgeted maintenance (planned 2026-09-05; branch `phase76-scale` from the Phase 75 close) → CLOSED 2026-09-06: vector scan (100k p50 393 ms, p95 documented), quality curve to 100k (gate met marginally: −0.10 from 159 → 100k, flat past 1k), full dream off the default path by ablation

Facts before planning (Rule 1, read from the code and the record): `HMGGraph._load` reads EVERY point and edge into
Python dicts at start-up; `retrieve_memory` is a pure-Python cosine scan over all active points (Phase 30.5, on the
Phase 30 code: p95 8 ms at 500 points → 575 ms at 50k, linear; the 500 ms budget crossed at ~40–50k) and Phase 74.7
added one `relevance_gate` (a cosine) per candidate edge in `_best_edge_toward`; numpy is NOT in the venv (a
vectorised scan is a dependency decision, not a given); the dream loop runs seven stages (macros, super-macros,
wormholes, contradictions, decay, promotion, rebalance, insights) with budgets on only two of them (`max_pairs`,
`max_checks`) and no time or token budget; E.2 recorded that the oracle setting "does not test retrieval-at-scale" —
the confound this phase measures. Programme row 76: a 100k-point synthetic graph with a latency/quality curve; dreams
redefined as budgeted Fu-R maintenance (propose relations · verify dependencies · rebuild derived caches) kept in the
default path only if the ablation shows "recall unchanged, tokens −x%".

Rules of the phase: measure first, then one move at a time, each gated; benches on throwaway DBs; production DB never
touched; a new dependency only if the measured curve requires it and the decision is written down.

## Phase 72 — M3: assertions with entities, modality and time (Fu-R schema) (2026-09-05; branch `phase72-assertions`)
Codex's findings D/E (still open after Phases 69–71) and the Fu-R proposal (`docs/FU_R_VS_FU2_ANALYSIS.md`): the ledger loses the SUBJECT and the CONTEXT of a statement — single quotes and fiction across sentences change the user's name, "recipe link" overwrites the car link, the mapper binds a value from another clause, two dogs share one slot, a legacy pet value survives a correction, "desde 2023" is treated as past. Design (Rules 3/4/5): **E/C/R objects on top of the existing ledger, as views** — E = the episode (already stored), C = an assertion record `(entity_id, relation, value, polarity, modality, valid_from, valid_to, recorded_at, source episode/span, status)`, R = a justification `(conclusion, premises AND/OR, type, status)` — kept in a new `assertions` module; `canonical_facts` remains the single-valued compatibility view (a cardinality ordinal `<slot>.2` when the SAME message asserts two entities of the same kind); modality per SENTENCE with carry-over of a scope marker ("For a fictional character." → the next sentence is fiction); "since <year>" = current with `valid_from`; the update form binds only when its subject is ONLY generic words; the mapper's value must sit in the same clause as its relation cue; a named negation ("Teca, not Bento") retracts Bento in every pet slot; validity is evaluated at QUERY time — past-cue questions get a HISTORY line instead of a globally demoted memory. External gate: the 7 deferred M3 delta checks (`single_quote_scope`, `fiction_scope_across_sentences`, `current_pt_since_date`, `unrelated_recipe_link`, `mapper_relation_and_value_same_claim`, `two_entities_same_species`, `legacy_pet_current_consistency`) promoted in `expected.json`; write precision ≥ 98% / coverage ≥ 90% on a NEW sealed multilingual set.

## Phase 71 — M2: receipts per action, post-conditions per step (2026-09-05; branch `phase71-receipts`)
Codex's finding C (still open after Phase 70): "a tool ran" is confused with "this step was fulfilled" — `update_plan(done)` accepts any executed tool, `end_turn` matches tool NAMES not arguments, one write can complete two steps, done+failed finalizes as done, and nothing survives a crash between effect and receipt. Design (Rules 3/4): a **receipt** is written for every executed action (id, session, turn, plan step, tool, normalised args, authorization origin, started/finished, result summary, observed effects, verified post-condition, consumed_by step); a **step post-condition** is derived deterministically from the step text (files it names → exist with a content hash; "widget" → a widget receipt in this plan; a named tool → a successful receipt of that tool; otherwise any non-read receipt) and checked against the WORLD, not the trace; a receipt can be consumed by exactly one step. External gate: the 4 deferred M2 delta checks (`partial_failure_not_done`, `plan_evidence_binds_arguments`, `read_then_update_done_not_write_evidence`, `receipt_not_reused_for_next_step`) promoted in `expected.json`.

## Phase 70 — M0 + M1 of Codex's plan: immutable evidence, scoped authority (2026-09-05; branch `phase69-audit-response` → `phase70-authority-scope`)
Input: `docs/PHASE68_PLANO_MELHORIAS.md` (M0–M7) and `docs/PHASE69_REVALIDACAO_INDEPENDENTE.md`; external gate = `scripts/audit_phase69_delta.py` (35 checks, **3/35 on 8b1cc91**, reproduced by me). Scope = M0 (evidence and test environment) + M1 (authority per action with scope; revocation persists). Of the 35 delta checks, **18 belong to M0/M1** and must pass here: `shell_write_0..11`, `readonly_shell_control`, `unknown_skill_is_not_readonly_by_default`, `negative_instruction_closes_authority`, `resume_does_not_mint_approval`, `skill_dispatch_requires_effect_declaration`, `long_cancellation_revokes`; plus the two evaluator defects (`invented_entity_not_grounding`, `truth_contracted_negation`) taken into M0 as evidence integrity. The other 14 (receipts M2: `partial_failure_not_done`, `plan_evidence_binds_arguments`, `read_then_update_done_not_write_evidence`, `receipt_not_reused_for_next_step`; assertions M3: `single_quote_scope`, `fiction_scope_across_sentences`, `current_pt_since_date`, `unrelated_recipe_link`, `mapper_relation_and_value_same_claim`, `two_entities_same_species`, `legacy_pet_current_consistency`; target-bound claims M5: `same_class_wrong_target_claim`, `file_write_is_not_widget_creation`; controls) stay open by design and are NOT claimed. Decisions taken (Rules 3/13): (a) no shell parser — shell is an effect unless it matches a tiny allow-list GRAMMAR (single segment, known read-only program, known flags, no redirection/substitution/newline); reads go through native `list_files`/`read_file`; (b) authorization is a RECORD (origin, granting message, turn) bound to the plan, never a boolean — resume preserves, never mints; a legacy plan without a record is UNAPPROVED and asks; (c) prohibition and cancellation are state before the effect and win over router tools and keywords; (d) a tool without a declared effect (`x-effect` in its schema) is unknown → blocked without authorization; (e) the code-block materializer becomes a dispatched `write_file` with a trace entry (receipt), never a silent write.

## Phase 69 — Response to the Phase 68 re-audit: one authority boundary, evidence-bound claims, honest write side (2026-09-05; branch `phase69-audit-response`)
Context: Codex's independent re-audit (`docs/PHASE68_REAUDITORIA.md`, oracle `scripts/audit_phase68_contracts.py`) stopped at 00:40 on a usage limit with 68.5/68.6/68.8/68.9 open; its detailed plan file was never written. I re-ran its deterministic oracle myself on `04fc9ba`: **12/56 pass, reproduced exactly**. Independent verdict per failing check (Rules 1/2/13): **36 accepted** as real contract gaps; **5 downgraded** — `grounding_entity_binding`, `grounding_small_number`, `grounding_unknown_entity` ask a lexical gate for semantic entity binding (P2, documented limit, not fixed here), `two_pets` is a schema decision (species slots added with `pet.name` kept for compatibility), `bash_confirmation_boundary` needs a mutating-command classifier, not a blanket block (a read-only `ls` on a question turn must keep working — Phase 67 read_intent); **3 are benchmark-oracle defects** (`benchmark_failed_search_not_success`, `benchmark_negation_53/55`) fixed in the benches. Two findings of MY OWN from Codex's live turns (`outputs/phase68_live_memory.json`): (i) the say-do gate manufactured absurd PROPOSALS on plain memory acknowledgements ("I've noted your name…" → a "proposed" plan titled with the reply sentence) — a promise about remembering is fulfilled by the fact write, not a side effect; (ii) "Sim, podes avançar." was not recognised as approval (the yes-regex requires the message to end right after the yes-word). Design principle for every fix: **one authority boundary keyed on turn state and evidence — never on phrases in the reply**; production `hmgfu.db` never written by tests or benches.

## Phase 66 — Harnessed tool use: precise, grounded, minimal (planned 2026-09-04; research in `docs/PHASE66_HARNESS_RESEARCH.md`)
Case (session 8269adf1ef1047c4 T4 "tell me whats todays weather", records + UI): 4 tool rounds — hallucinated tool `weather` → tool_search → brave with the RAW sentence (no place) → generic US snippet → reply "26°C clear skies" (in NO tool output = output hallucination) + an unasked weather widget carrying that value. The June standing rule "always use brave for Valencia weather" is a memory (not a directive) and was dropped on the action turn. T3 "stop with the scientifics facts" cleared the closer deterministically while the model misread it as tone. Research verdict: harness design, not model size, decides tool precision for small models; the three hallucination classes (schema/argument/output) map 1:1 to this turn; grounding must be a runtime trace check, not a prompt line; constrain only the router (constraint tax).

## Phase 59 — EXTERNAL VALIDATION (does it generalize? is the embedder the bottleneck?)
Prompted by an external reviewer's ROADMAP critique (verified against the repo, Rule 1). The core honest gap: EVERY A/B that flatters Fu runs on a corpus WE wrote (Phase 30.1 = 26 hand-authored points, and 2 of its 4 categories — recency/contradiction — are things cosine CANNOT do by construction, so the 0.89-vs-0.56 headline is inflated by category selection, not just authorship). The two things we genuinely DON'T know: (a) does the field beat RAG on data we don't control, and (b) is nomic the cross-lingual bottleneck. HARD RULE for this phase: run each measurement ONCE, record it, walk away — the moment we retune weights to win an external benchmark we've reclosed the loop (Rule 3, our own rule).
- [x] **Exp 2 DONE (b4i2biual) — VERDICT: bge-m3 migration is LOAD-BEARING (hard proof, not a feeling).** `scripts/probe_crosslingual.py`, 12 PT/EN pairs through live nomic-embed-text: EN-CEIL (same-lang paraphrase) **0.923** · cross-lingual MATCH (PT vs its EN translation) **0.578** · X-FLOOR (unrelated) **0.377** → **retention = 37%** of the same-language span; worst pair AT the noise floor (0.381 vs 0.377). nomic nails English (0.92) but a PT sentence vs its EN twin is barely distinguishable from random → the collapse is SPECIFICALLY cross-lingual. Confirms [[pa3-multilingual-embedder]] with numbers. The PT symptom-fixes (phrase-learning, active-directive) were band-aids; the ROOT is the embedder. → schedule bge-m3/multilingual-e5 as its own phase (768→1024 re-embed migration). Caveat noted: EN-CEIL high means the verdict isn't a nomic-prefix artifact — it's genuine English-centricity.
- [x] **Exp 1 DONE (bfiz3umyv, N=100, 1140-paragraph HotpotQA corpus) — VERDICT: the Fu field does NOT beat RAG on foreign data. Cosine WINS on every metric.** OVERALL support_recall@10 FU 0.940 vs BASE **0.955**, full_support FU 0.880 vs BASE **0.920**, MRR FU 0.825 vs BASE **0.936**. bridge: FU 0.930 vs BASE 0.943. **BRIDGE-HOP recall@10 (the multi-hop test expand_through_fu should win): FU 0.873 vs BASE 0.899 — cosine wins even here.** Sensitizer degradation negligible (3 timeouts/1 fallback of 1140), so NOT an excuse. INTERPRETATION (honest, not spin): (a) CONFIRMED — "relational field beats vector search" does NOT generalize; the 0.89-vs-0.56 headline was an artifact of our 26-pt curated corpus + 2 categories cosine can't do by construction. The big MRR gap = Fu's importance/recency/energy weighting adds RANKING NOISE on a static corpus. (b) NOT tested — HotpotQA is static (no time/supersession); Fu's actual domain is personal/temporal memory → fair test = a LONGITUDINAL external set (LoCoMo/MSC), still open. (c) Strategic: HMG-Fu's value is likely in the TEMPORAL/facts/agentic layers (Phase 30.4 ablation: deterministic keyed supersession adds guaranteed contradiction-resolution), NOT generic retrieval ranking. RECORDED AS-IS, no retuning (Rule 3). Harness: scripts/bench_ab_hotpot.py; data scratch/hotpot_slice.json.
- [ ] (open) Exp 1b — the FAIR test of Fu's actual domain: a longitudinal/multi-session external set (LoCoMo / Multi-Session Chat) with real temporal structure, so recency/supersession are exercised (not neutralized as in HotpotQA). Same run-once-no-tuning discipline.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: another feature, widget, or A/B on our own data — building on the closed loop tells us nothing new.

### SCIENTIFIC diagnosis — WHY Fu loses to cosine on retrieval (user: "sem consolo, análise científica")
- [x] Quantified from the ACTUAL weights (hmgfu/config.py MEMORY_SCORE_WEIGHTS, sum=0.95): `semantic`=0.42 (itself 0.75·cosine+0.25·lexical) · `kappa`=0.20 · `modeMatch`=0.08 · `recency`=0.07 · `wormhole`=0.07 · `density`=0.06 · `utility`=0.05. **Pure cosine is only ≈33% of Fu's ranking signal** (0.42×0.75/0.95); baseline is 100% cosine. The other ~67% (lexical, kappa entity/topic overlap, density hub-boost, recency, modeMatch) is uncorrelated-to-harmful on a STATIC corpus → dilutes the cosine signal → gold demoted → MRR 0.936→0.825. Mechanism of the bridge-hop loss: `lexical_relevance` = query-token coverage; a bridge gold shares FEW words with the question → the 0.25·lexical term penalizes it while rewarding word-overlap distractors.
- [x] Hypothesis TESTED & FALSIFIED (honesty): suspected score saturation/clamp→ties. REFUTED — weights sum 0.95, all HotpotQA points source="user" (factor 1.0) → raw ≤ 0.95 < 1.0, no clamp. Not the cause.
- [x] CONCLUSION (no consolation): you cannot beat pure cosine on GENERIC retrieval without raising semantic→1.0 and dropping kappa/recency/density — i.e. becoming cosine. Those terms ARE Fu; on a corpus with no temporal/relational structure they can only subtract. HotpotQA correctly showed Fu is not a generic-RAG-beater (never its claim). Two DOMAIN-INDEPENDENT precision levers worth an honest A/B (help everywhere without gutting Fu): (1) make the 0.25·lexical a tie-breaker/exact-ID gate, not a 25% blend (it penalizes lexically-distant-but-correct answers); (2) a retrieval-mode that raises semantic when the query has no temporal/personal signal (detection is the risk). Speed: Fu = 6 O(N) channels + per-candidate rich score (incl. a lexical token-scan) + expand_through_fu traversal ≈ 6–10× cosine's single pass; faster = fewer channels/expansion = fewer Fu features. Both speed & precision trade against the machinery.
- [x] CONFIRMING experiment DONE (bf587f7z4, scripts/diag_fu_vs_cosine.py, N=60): of 120 gold instances, **44 demoted by Fu below cosine**. Mean weighted-contribution Δ (promoter − gold) per term: **kappa +0.0168 (#1, 38% of the +0.044 gap)** · semantic-blend +0.0131 (30%) · fuDistancePenalty +0.0081 (18%) · rest ~0.006. PROVEN: the demotion is driven by `kappa` (entity/topic overlap — HotpotQA's hard distractors are topically related → kappa boosts them over the bridge gold that shares fewer entities), then the lexical part of the semantic blend (pure cosine favours the gold by definition of "demotion", yet the blend favours the promoter → its higher query-word overlap outweighs lower cosine = lever-1's lexical dilution caught live), then the hex-distance penalty on the relationally-farther gold. CONCLUSION HARDENED: kappa IS the field; down-weighting it = becoming cosine. Even a perfect lever-1 fix leaves Fu losing on HotpotQA. These terms are signal ONLY on temporal/personal data → Exp 1b (LoCoMo) is decisive, not HotpotQA.
- [x] CRITIQUE ACCEPTED (Trailblazer, Rule 2/13 self-correction): my "can't beat cosine without becoming cosine" CONFLATED kappa-as-ranking-term with the field itself. WRONG. The fix is DECOUPLING, not surrender: rank by pure cosine, then APPEND the Fu entity-hop expansion BELOW the cosine winners (append-only → can only add, never tax). My own data supports it — 76/120 golds Fu ranked ≥ cosine, and comparison 1.000→0.976 proves the FUSED field can only TAX no-hop cases. I omitted the decoupled architecture from the options — that was the miss. Also mis-scoped two terms: (a) `fuDistancePenalty` (18% of gap) is NOT intrinsic Fu — on a static batch-ingested corpus hex-distance has no relevance signal (like recency); it should be OFF for non-personal retrieval = probably the cheapest win; (b) the semantic-blend split (30%) SIZES lever 1 and I under-called it. KEY REFRAME: architecture (decouple) is decidable NOW on HotpotQA; the THESIS (Fu terms become signal on temporal data) needs LoCoMo — TWO decisions, don't run the thesis test on an architecture I already have evidence to change (unfalsifiable-thesis trap).
- [ ] SEQUENCED PLAN (post-promotion, all on the bge-m3 graph so the cosine BASE is definitive — a moved baseline invalidates the A/B; re-run pure-cosine BASE on bge-m3, never compare vs the old nomic BASE = "two embedders as one"). **ATTRIBUTION DISCIPLINE (Trailblazer pt 2): ONE change, ONE measurement — running decouple + distance-off + lever-1 together repeats the fused-problem at the experiment level (a positive can't say which helped, a negative can't say which sank it). Order below isolates each effect as a delta over the previous.**
  1. (needs GPU — re-ingest on bge-m3; the N=60 throwaway db was deleted) two measurements: (i) pure-cosine rank of the missing BRIDGE doc in bridge-fail cases — rank 15-40 → hybrid has headroom to win bridge; rank 200+ → append only ties BASE; (ii) split the semantic-blend Δ (0.0131) into cosine-contribution vs lexical-contribution → sizes lever 1.
  2. **BASE anchor**: fresh pure-cosine on the bge-m3 graph (the number everything else is measured against).
  3. **Decouple ALONE**: rank by cosine, append Fu entity-hop expansion BELOW the cosine winners (no top reorder) → measure vs #2. Isolates the ARCHITECTURE effect. (Expansion-edge threshold is a variable, per the +21%-edges nuance.)
  → [x] DONE (bcxjp4qmt, N=100 on bge-m3): **DECOUPLE does NOT rescue the field on HotpotQA — negative result, accepted.** Decisive measurement: the 8 bridge golds cosine misses @10 all sit at cosine-rank ≤40 (median 17) — BUT pure cosine already recovers them at deeper k (base recall@20 0.985, @30 0.995); NO deep gold (rank 100+) for a Fu-hop to rescue. A/B: recall@10 identical (dec keeps cosine top-10); recall@20 base 0.985 → dec **0.970**, @30 0.995 → dec **0.980** — the append HURTS by displacing the genuine cosine-rank-11-40 near-miss golds with topological neighbours (which aren't the golds). Best-case decouple (append at the very bottom) would TIE, never beat — no relevance signal the cosine lacks. So the field is not a retrieval win in ANY architecture (fused=tax, decoupled=displace/tie) on generic multi-hop QA. **Independent win: bge-m3 lifted the cosine BASELINE itself — bridge MRR 0.936(nomic)→0.960(bge-m3), recall@10 0.943→0.949 — the embedder helped retrieval directly.** steps 4/5 (fuDistancePenalty-off, lever-1) are now moot for BEATING cosine here (they'd only narrow a gap in the FUSED score, which we're abandoning as a ranking mechanism); keep lever-1/distance-off as clean-ups for the personal-memory (temporal) path if the thesis test warrants. ### Exp 1b — LoCoMo (temporal-retrieval thesis test). TWO GATES pre-registered BEFORE building (Trailblazer discipline).
- FRAMING (fixed, Trailblazer correction to my over-reaching headline): LoCoMo decides ONE of HMG-Fu's TWO theses, NOT a verdict on the project. A retrieval win died on static data; a DETERMINISTIC win is ALIVE and NOT on trial here — already measured: Phase 30.4 ablation (substrate 78% vs canon 100% on contradiction-resolution, deficit isolated to directive-supersession) + directive follow/change/clear cycle 6/6 multilingual + bge-m3 lifting the cosine BASELINE itself (bridge MRR 0.936→0.960, shipped). LoCoMo measures STRICTLY: do the temporal score terms (recency, supersession-in-ranking) beat pure cosine on multi-session recall? A negative kills the temporal-RETRIEVAL leg only — HMG-Fu remains a real deterministic-memory system with a working cross-lingual embedder regardless.
- **GATE 1 — falsifiability PRE-COMMITTED (before a single number): a NEGATIVE LoCoMo result FALSIFIES the temporal-retrieval thesis. No escape hatch ("afinal não é bem memória pessoal"). We spent the whole session disciplining against "the test that would vindicate me is the one I haven't run" — LoCoMo counts as arbiter ONLY under this pre-commitment. ACCEPTED.**
- **GATE 2 — labels are the benchmark's, not self-derived → clean arbiter (VERIFIED on the real data, scratch/locomo10.json from snap-research/locomo):** 10 dated multi-session conversations; each `qa` item ships `{question, answer, evidence, category}` where `evidence` names the exact gold turn(s) (e.g. `['D1:3']`). So the retrieval gold is GIVEN, not derived → as hard as HotpotQA (no derivation bias). PASS. (Had it been self-derived, we'd have flagged it "indicative, not decisive" per the gate.)
- HARNESS DESIGN (both gates green): ingest each dialogue turn as a point with its SESSION DATE as the timestamp (so recency/temporal terms have a real axis — the thing HotpotQA lacked); query = the QA question; gold = the `evidence` turn ids; EXCLUDE category 5 (adversarial/unanswerable — no retrievable gold). BASE = FRESH pure-cosine on bge-m3 (never an old number). Measure recall@k / MRR: Fu-fused vs BASE, and Fu-decoupled vs BASE as SEPARATE measurements (attribution discipline). Rule 3: NO retuning temporal terms to flatter LoCoMo — if Fu wins, it wins with the config already in production.
- **GATE 3 RESOLVED (recency window) — run BOTH A and B side-by-side; the A−B gap IS the measurement of the recency term's contribution (the term under trial), per attribution discipline:** `recency_score = exp(-age/τ)`, τ=14 days. LoCoMo dates = May 2023 (~1150d) → recency ≈ 0 identically for every turn. **B = RAW dates** (recency dead — Fu as literally configured on literal 2023 data). **A = RE-BASED timeline** — shift ALL session dates by a SINGLE CONSTANT delta so the last session ≈ now; this PRESERVES the real inter-session gaps EXACTLY (constant shift = gaps unchanged) and only moves the temporal ORIGIN into the 14-day active window. CRITICAL (Trailblazer): shift origin YES, COMPRESS gaps NO — compressing would inject signal and make A unclean. Isolation: ingest once (edges/embeddings held constant), toggle only p.timestamp raw↔rebased at query time so the A−B delta is PURELY the recency term (supersession-by-time included: a fact stated session-3 and corrected session-15 is exactly where recency-alive should win). Rule 3: τ stays 14 (production config); we move the data into the window, not the knob.
- **GATE 4 (Trailblazer, the HotpotQA lesson transported) — PER-CATEGORY from the first number; cat 2 (temporal) is THE decisive line.** Aggregate recall would dilute the temporal signal exactly as HotpotQA-aggregate hid bridge-vs-comparison. Category map VERIFIED by reading questions: cat1=multi-hop, **cat2=temporal ("when…?"→dates)**, cat3=open-domain, cat4=single-hop, cat5=adversarial/unanswerable (EXCLUDED). **Sample-size check (the pre-build question) ANSWERED: cat2 = 321 temporal Qs total, 24–42 per conversation → DOZENS, the decisive line HOLDS WEIGHT (not a noisy handful).** Falsifiability (Gate 1) applies to cat 2 specifically: a negative on cat 2 WITH recency alive (config A, fair window) falsifies the temporal-retrieval thesis, period.
- [x] **DONE (b7xy9n8ws, N=3, bge-m3) — TEMPORAL-RETRIEVAL THESIS FALSIFIED (Gate 1 honored, no escape).** Decisive cat2 (TEMPORAL, n=90, recency ALIVE/fair window): **BASE cosine MRR 0.408 vs Fu-A 0.222** (~2× worse); recall@5 0.611 vs 0.267, @10 0.744 vs 0.456, @20 0.844 vs 0.656. Fu-A does NOT beat BASE on cat2 → thesis FALSIFIED per the pre-registration. Not close, not only temporal — cosine crushes Fu on EVERY category (cat1 MRR .232 vs .059, cat4 .329 vs .166, cat3 .107 vs .034). Recency DID contribute (Fu-A .222 > Fu-B .195, +0.027 MRR — the mechanism fires) but it's a rounding error vs the 0.19 gap. Mechanism of the loss (same as HotpotQA, worse on the larger ~400-700-turn pool): Fu's 6-channel candidate-gathering narrows the pool before scoring AND the memory_score terms (kappa/density/recency) dilute the semantic signal → the specific answer-turn gets demoted. n=90 with a ~2× effect is decisive; N=10 would confirm direction, not flip it.
- [x] **VERDICT (sem consolo, correctly scoped): the "relational field beats RAG" RETRIEVAL thesis is DEAD across all domains + architectures** — static QA (HotpotQA: fused taxes, decoupled displaces/ties) AND temporal multi-session (LoCoMo: cosine ~2× better even with recency alive). No evidence anywhere supports field-as-retrieval. **What SURVIVES, proven + untouched by this:** (1) the DETERMINISTIC facts/directives layer — Phase 30.4 ablation substrate 78% vs canon 100% on contradiction-resolution + directive cycle 6/6 multilingual; (2) bge-m3 shipped, lifting the cosine baseline itself (bridge MRR 0.936→0.960) + fixing PT↔EN recall 37%→100% — live in production. A leg died; the system stands on the other, proven leg. HMG-Fu = a real DETERMINISTIC memory-management + agentic system with a working cross-lingual embedder — NOT a better retriever. This is the science the whole gate discipline existed to protect: a clean, pre-registered falsification on a fair test.
  4. **fuDistancePenalty OFF** as a delta over #3 (cheapest win, 18%; on a static batch corpus hex-distance has no relevance signal, like recency).
  5. **Lever 1** (0.25·lexical → tie-breaker/exact-ID gate) as a delta over #4 (domain-independent; lexical must never demote a semantically-correct answer — helps personal memory too).
  6. THEN Exp 1b (LoCoMo) — the thesis test, on the corrected architecture. (Correction to pt 1's "no-GPU": the diagnostic's throwaway corpus is gone, so #1 does need a re-ingest; still cheap, run-once.)

## Phase 57 RESULT: replicable 34/34 achieved, zero prompt patches
Root cause of the ceiling was a DECODE-CHANNEL gap (loose `format="json"`), fixed structurally with Ollama schema-constrained decoding (enums from the live catalog — 100% dynamic). Evidence chain: probe 40/40 vs 24/40 → bench 32→33→**34/34 ×3**. Every fix root-caused with a regression test (269 offline tests). Deferred as own phases (NOT needed for gemma 34/34): P2b two-stage constrained tool-arg emit, P3 bge-m3 embedder, P6 Zep-style bi-temporal validity — cross-model robustness + durability enhancements.
**META — replicability harness:** upgrade bench to MULTI-SAMPLE (each check N times → per-decision pass-rate), proving replicability not single-sample luck.

Handoff investigation (Rule 1/2, no duplication): Codex built runtime_context.py (per-turn clock injected into chat + nano), turn_router.py (multilingual model routing, no English regexes), action_policy.py (exact-name structural fallback only), sensitizer routing, and the qwen/gemma-cpu role split. Deployed server (pid 46760, 03:36) already runs the new code + config.
- [x] A. Verified current state: offline 200/200; deployed config = role split; runtime clock wired into chat system prompt (agent.py:230, chat.py:114); benchmark has 33 mandatory checks incl. clock (L19/L20) + multilingual (L21-L25).
- [x] B. Full 34-check cloned-live benchmark ran to completion: 32/34. Structural S1-S7 PASS; clock L19/L20 PASS (exact +02:00 local, EN+PT); multilingual proactivity L21-L24 PASS; correction/session L17/L18 PASS (Codex's stall point cleared). ONLY L6/L7 failed (explicit English command not executed).
- [x] B1. Root-caused L6/L7 (Rule 2/13): NOT a logic bug — re-ran L6 in isolation 4/4 PASS (act_req=True, req_tools=['bash'], USED=['bash']). Failure = transient Ollama degradation under sustained 4-model load (empty-response). EXACT bug: OllamaClient.chat (ollama_client.py:59) + OllamaProvider.chat (providers.py:99) return a 200 EMPTY-content response as success with no retry; only embed() checks empty. So a momentary thrash silently zeroes the routing signal → action_requested defaults False → no enforcement → prose.
- [x] B2. Resilience hardening (still valid): ollama_client.chat + providers.OllamaProvider.chat retry empty-content 200s 3× with 0.6/1.2s backoff (mirror embed()); provider keeps a legitimate tool-only turn. tests/test_v15_ollama_resilience.py (4 tests).
- [x] B3. TRUE L6/L7 root cause (re-run showed 0 empty responses yet L6/L7 still failed): a conversation_opener directive in the SYSTEM PROMPT forces the model into text-generation mode → it tells a joke + "I will run it" and never emits the tool call. Reproduced deterministically (with the opener active, L6 fails isolated AND in-seq; response is the joke). This is THE user's "not proactive" defect when a joke-opener is set.
- [x] B4. Fix (agent.py, Rule 13): for action-required turns keep the opener OUT of the prompt (opener_in_prompt = not requested_actions and first_turn) so the model tool-calls; the deterministic enforce() still prepends the opener to the final answer, so the directive is honoured either way. LIVE-verified: L6 isolated + in-seq now bash_used=True, output_in_answer=True, opener_present=True ("Why did the scarecrow… \n\n The output is PROACTIVE-FU-51"). tests/test_v16_opener_proactivity.py (2 tests: opener out-of-prompt for action turns, in-prompt for plain first turn).
- [x] B5. Offline suite 206/206. Benchmark re-run STILL failed L6/L7 with 0 empty responses AND no joke — so neither resilience nor opener was the benchmark's L6 cause.
- [x] B6. TRUE benchmark-L6 root cause (evidenced): production has only output_suffix:Trailblazer (no opener). The nano/main ROUTER is non-deterministic — ~1 in 4 it mislabels "Run the shell command …" as conversation_act=statement + action_requested=False, and Codex's semantic action-recovery (tool_points.py:99) was gated on conv_act=="instruction" only → recovery skipped → zero tools offered → action lost → "I will execute" prose. Calibration: actions score 0.39-0.46 on their real tool, questions 0.32-0.37 on spurious tools; a misroute lands as 'statement', never 'question'.
- [x] B7. Fix (tool_points.py, Rule 13): broaden the recovery gate to conv_act in ("instruction","statement") — rescues misrouted commands while questions/greetings/feedback stay tool-free (preserves L1/L2 precision + L3 identity, which relies on retrieved NOT being cleared). LIVE-verified: benchmark-L6 sequence 6/6 bash executed + output in answer. tests/test_v17_action_recovery.py (3 tests).
- [x] B8. FINAL live benchmark = 34/34 FAIL=0 on gemma4:12b (1508-node clone). L6/L7 bash proactive, L10 create_widget, L17 correction+opener, L19/L20 exact clock EN+PT, L21 PT proactive bash — ALL PASS. Offline 209/209.
- [x] C. Deployed server restarted onto the fixed code (pid stopped, preview_start fresh). LIVE deployed verify: "what is the exact current time right now?" → "It is currently 10:40 AM on July 5, 2026" (correct, matches host clock, 0 tools). RuntimeContext.capture() = host clock exactly. Residual: routing is non-deterministic (~1 in 4) — one clock phrasing misrouted to brave_web_search + a wrong minute; same routing-classification ceiling the recovery mitigates but cannot fully remove with local models. Scratch clones cleaned; production hmgfu.db untouched (21.7MB).

## Phase 27 — Temporal perception + memory correctness (Sebastian audit)
Investigation (Rule 1/2) — 3 confirmed root causes behind the "Your name is Sebastian" pollution:
- [x] Injection has NO temporal labels/ordering (retrieve.organise_for_injection lists bare lines) → LLM can't tell old wrong facts from the newer correction
- [x] ingest_memory has NO dedup → 4× "Your name is Sebastian" as separate fact nodes
- [x] _should_store_assistant stores any reply of type=fact → "Done, I've remembered your name is Sebastian" becomes a NEW fact (assistant self-poisoning feedback loop, PA3-documented)
- [x] Confirmed cross-session: screenshots are different sessions; correction DID propagate via a global macro (memory is global by design) — but raw wrong facts persisted
### Fixes
- [x] A. Temporal awareness: fu_math.age_label (just now/Nm/Nh/Nd/Nw/Nmo/Ny) tags every injected hex; newest-first ordering within sections; header "TRUST THE MOST RECENT, treat older as superseded" (retrieve.py)
- [x] B. Dedup at ingest: _find_duplicate (same-kind, cosine ≥ DEDUP_MIN_COSINE=0.94) → reinforce+return one node; embedding computed once and reused (ingest.py)
- [x] C. Assistant self-poisoning fixed: _store_assistant_reply (base, both call sites) NEVER stores as fact (mtype=message) + skips echoes of recalled memories (cosine ≥ 0.9); removed duplicated store logic (Rule 5)
- [x] D. Loose-ends sweep: found+fixed dedup negation-merge risk (polarity guard: "X" vs "not X" never merge); confirmed macros/tool-points bypass dedup, single assistant-store path
- [x] E. Tests: 8 temporal/correctness tests; 120 green
- [x] E2. Live repro (round 1) exposed the DEEPER root cause: nano summary DROPPED the value ("My name is Teodoro Ferreira" → "corrects an identity"), so the model never saw "Teodoro" and answered "I don't know your name". Temporal labels help reasoning but don't restore lost values.
### Root-cause fix — first-class facts (PA3 hmg_fact_statements analog, #1 parity gap)
- [x] hmgfu/facts.py — detect_fact (name / "my X is Y" / call-me, multi-clause negation-aware: "I'm not Sebastian. My name is Teodoro" → name=Teodoro supersedes=Sebastian); FactStore keyed by concept, NEW value deterministically supersedes OLD (PRIMARY KEY), persists across sessions
- [x] Injected VERBATIM at the front ("Your name is Teodoro Ferreira (corrected from Sebastian)") — never the lossy summary; retrieve.build_llm_context gains canonical param
- [x] supersede_stale_nodes: old-value episodic nodes marked superseded → drop from recall
- [x] Wired in AgentEngine (apply per turn, supersede, inject canonical); /api/facts endpoint (Rule 10)
- [x] Tests: 5 fact tests (detection, keyed supersession+persistence, verbatim render w/ correction, agent e2e supersede+inject, negation-clears-matching); 126 green; agent.py held at 400 ceiling
- [x] E3. Live repro (round 2) PASS: canonical fact name=Teodoro Ferreira (prev Sebastian), 0 stale active Sebastian nodes, gemma answered "Your name is Teodoro Ferreira." to "what is my name?"

## Phase 30 — Prove/disprove the four unproven theory claims (A/B, wormhole, ablation, scale)
User asked to try to PROVE (or honestly disprove) four specific open claims from the Phase-29 report. Investigation first (Rule 1/2): read fu_math.py (memory_score §30, kappa §7, wormhole §17 thresholds), retrieve.py (6-channel retrieval + expand_through_fu), dream.py (should_create_wormhole/analogy_heuristic), store.py (graph API), propagate.py, chat.py (base HMGFuEngine has NO facts/directives — the pure-Fu-substrate condition for ablation), config.py (WORMHOLE thresholds: hexDist>5, analogy>0.7, utility/novelty gates, semantic>0.42, entityOverlap<0.5, topicOverlap>=0.25).
- [x] 30.1 A/B retrieval benchmark (scripts/bench_ab_retrieval.py) — 26-point real corpus (real embeddings + real nano sensitizer), baseline=plain cosine top-k (bench-only, never used in production), Fu=production retrieve_memory(); 9 labeled queries across direct/relational/recency/contradiction categories; hit@1, hit@3, MRR per category
- [x] 30.2 Run + record results with evidence (no cherry-picking) — **RESULT: baseline WON overall (MRR 0.76 vs Fu 0.58)**. Category breakdown: relational (the one category Fu is specifically built for) Fu wins 0.75 vs 0.67 MRR — expand_through_fu's entity-hop genuinely surfaced "Leo's teacher" and "Daniel's book" via same_entity/goal_related edges baseline couldn't reach. But direct-control Fu LOST (0.75 vs 1.00 — should have been a trivial tie) and recency/contradiction Fu also lost or tied (0.50/0.25 vs 0.75/0.50) despite recency/tension terms existing specifically for those cases.
  ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, not guessed — score breakdown dumped for every miss, Rule 1/2/13): a small sub-cluster of memories (Leo/reading-tutor/Daniel's-chess-book) built up mutually-reinforcing same_entity/goal_related/part_of edges and high nano-assigned utility (0.90), which raised their ρ (density, driven partly by κ-weighted centrality) enough that they out-scored the ACTUAL correct memory for entirely unrelated queries (marathon goal, cat's name, spicy food, coffee) even though the correct memory's raw semantic cosine was clearly higher (0.78, 0.76, 0.75, 0.67 vs unlisted-but-lower competitor cosines). Two compounding factors: (1) MEMORY_SCORE_WEIGHTS gives density 0.18 + kappa 0.17 + utility 0.14 = 0.49 combined weight vs semantic's 0.24 — a well-connected hub can out-mass topical relevance; (2) query_kappa() ALSO contains its own 0.25-weighted cosine term, so semantic similarity is counted twice but through two different-sized weights, diluting rather than reinforcing its discriminative power. This is a genuine, reproducible finding — NOT fixed unilaterally (retuning MEMORY_SCORE_WEIGHTS to make this benchmark look better would itself be a symptom patch on my own eval, Rule 3); flagged for the user as the highest-priority actionable lead from this whole sweep.
- [x] 30.3 Wormhole live-fire test (scripts/bench_wormhole_live.py) — 35 real-ingested statements (real gemma-adjacent nano extraction) across 7 unrelated domains incl. 3 planted cross-domain analogies (guitar/Spanish "daily practice beats weekend cramming"). RESULT: 0 wormholes fired, confirming the claim. Root-cause diagnosis (not contrived): the closest planted pair — "skipping guitar practice" <-> "missing spanish practice" — passed 5/7 gates (analogy=0.73>0.7, semantic=0.73, utility/novelty/entityOverlap all OK) but was blocked by (a) hexDistance=4, needs >5 (1 short — the graph is too young/small for centroid placement to spread same-density points that far apart) and (b) topicOverlap=0.00, needs >=0.25 (nano labeled the two as "effectiveness/habit" vs "learning habits" — semantically identical, lexically disjoint tags, Jaccard=0). FINDING: topicOverlap-via-literal-tag-Jaccard is in tension with the analogy heuristic's own definition ("structural similarity WITH lexical dissimilarity") — a genuine cross-domain analogy is disproportionately likely to have non-overlapping topic labels. Not fixed unilaterally (design-threshold decision, flagged for user)
- [x] 30.4 Ablation test (scripts/bench_ablation.py) — identical fact-correction + directive-obedience + directive-contradiction scenarios through SUBSTRATE (chat.HMGFuEngine, no facts/directives/hygiene) vs CANON (agent.AgentEngine) on real gemma. Ran 3x (gemma temp=0.6 → real run-to-run variance, so n=1 would be unreliable evidence). RESULT aggregate over 3 trials (9 checks each): SUBSTRATE 7/9 (78%), CANON 9/9 (100%). Per-scenario breakdown pinpoints WHERE: fact-correction 3/3 and single-directive-obedience 3/3 passed even in pure substrate (plain associative recall + recency is often enough); the deficit is concentrated entirely in directive-CONTRADICTION resolution (old directive fully overridden by a newer one) — SUBSTRATE only 1/3 there vs CANON 3/3. CONFIRMS the claim with precision: the field gives good-enough recall most of the time, but deterministic keyed supersession is specifically what turns contradiction-resolution from probabilistic into guaranteed — matching the original Phase 27 root cause almost exactly
- [x] 30.5 Scale test (scripts/bench_scale.py) — synthetic seeding 500..50k points, retrieve_memory() wall-clock, 8 probes/size. RESULT: 500pts=8.1ms, 1k=12.9ms, 2.5k=28ms, 5k=57.5ms, 10k=100.1ms, 20k=232.7ms, 50k=574.5ms (p95). Linear scaling confirmed (70.6x latency growth vs 100x corpus growth). 500ms budget crossed at ~40-50k points — REVISES the "needs indexing around 10k+" claim: 10k is fine (100ms), the real inflection is ~4-5x higher than estimated
- [x] 30.6 Document all four results honestly — done above per-item. Summary of the four original claims after real measurement:
  1. "Field beats RAG is architecture not evidence" → NOW HAS EVIDENCE, and it's MIXED-NEGATIVE overall: Fu wins decisively on relational multi-hop (its actual design target), but LOSES to plain cosine on direct/recency/contradiction due to a diagnosed hub-dilution effect in MEMORY_SCORE_WEIGHTS. This is the single most important finding of the sweep.
  2. "Wormholes never fired live" → CONFIRMED, with a precise near-miss diagnosis (analogy heuristic and hex-distance/topic-overlap gates are in tension for genuine cross-domain analogies).
  3. "Canon layers give guarantees, field gives associative recall" → CONFIRMED with numbers: substrate-only 78% vs canon 100% over 3 real-gemma trials, deficit isolated to directive-contradiction resolution specifically.
  4. "Scale needs indexing ~10k+" → REVISED: measured linear scaling, actual 500ms-budget crossover is ~40-50k points, not 10k (10k measured at 100ms, comfortably fine).
  No source code in hmgfu/ was modified this phase — all four are new scripts/bench_*.py (throwaway .db files, gitignored). Full suite re-confirmed 134/134 after adding them.

### Wormhole root-cause analysis (why 0 form) — Rule 1/2, evidenced
1. **Young/synthetic graph (Phase 30):** `minTopicOverlap>=0.25` + `minHexDistance>5` blocked genuine cross-domain analogies (disjoint topic tags, small grid). FIXED (gates relaxed).
2. **Mature graph (this phase):** `minNovelty>0.5`/`minUtility>0.6` blocked ALL 5 gate-passing pairs — established imported identity memories aren't "novel", yet wormholes exist to connect exactly those. Internal contradiction with THEORY issue 10. FIXED (gate on density, not novelty).
3. **Deeper, remaining limitation (documented, NOT hacked):** the embedding-cosine analogy heuristic MIS-RANKS candidates — short generic conversational nodes score analogy 0.8+ (and are correctly nano-vetoed), while genuine cross-domain analogies score only ~0.43–0.47 with real nomic embeddings (below the 0.7 gate), so the nano judge never even evaluates them. The candidate-SURFACING signal (cosine) is the bottleneck, not the gates. A proper fix needs a structural-analogy surfacing signal or broader nano sampling — deferred as a design item rather than force a wormhole on this corpus (Rule 3).

## Phase 47 — Recall relevance (kill hub-bias) + visibility of recalled tools/skills/directives
User: "recalled memories are not relatable with my input" + "can i see what tools, skills and directives are being recalled?"
Root cause (Rule 1/2, evidenced by live score decomposition): memory_score let the ρ(density 0.18)+U(utility 0.14) "general importance" terms (sum 0.32) dominate semantic (0.24). A few dense identity hubs (Trailblazing ρ=0.90/U=0.99) maxed ρ/U and hijacked EVERY query regardless of meaning — e.g. "weather" recalled Trailblazing(sem 0.35) over the actual forecast; "brave search" recalled it over the sem=1.00 Brave node. (Echo filter correctly drops the user's own verbatim question nodes at cos≥0.93 — not the bug.)
- [x] A. Root cause proven: live decomposition showed off-topic hubs winning on ρ+U (0.30) vs semantic (0.10); pure-semantic top-5 (the SHOULD-surface set) buried below identity hubs
- [x] B. Fix = relevance gate in fu_math.memory_score: (ρ·γ + U·δ) scaled by imp_gate = clamp((rel-floor)/(ref-floor)), rel = max(semantic, query_kappa) — QUERY-RELATIVE ONLY (never edge.kappa, which any hub maxes out). config.IMPORTANCE_RELEVANCE_GATE = {floor 0.25, ref 0.50}
- [x] C. Identity never lost: rides the verbatim canonical-fact channel (facts.render_lines→userIdentity) + scores high on identity queries anyway
- [x] D. Calibrated with data (not guessed): swept floor/ref against BOTH real embedder (junk demoted, identity kept) AND fake-embedder tests (Sebastian sem 0.50→gate 1.0; Baltazar entity-match q_rel 0.458→gate 0.83, score 0.367>0.35). floor .28/ref .72 was too aggressive (killed legit recall); .25/.50 is the safe point
- [x] E. Evidence: 169/169 tests green; LIVE gated retrieve — "brave search" top6 all brave decisions (Trailblazing GONE); "weather" surfaces the real forecast session nodes (junk GONE); "my name?" identity preserved (Name Check sem 0.89 rose #6→#3)
- [x] F. Visibility: agent.py emits per-turn `context_pack` (tools / skills / directives, skill vs builtin split by tools.skill_handlers); events.jsx pushContext + case; Transcript.jsx ContextPill (expandable, hammer/box/shield icons). LIVE-verified in browser: pill "recalled 7 tools · 3 skills · 1 directive" renders under the memories pill; expanded shows gog_* as skills, web_search/create_widget/memory_* as tools, output_suffix:Trailblazer as directive. Two root causes (Rule 1/2, from logs + code): (A) BACKEND — the model over-planned and RE-CALLED plan_task in a loop (it has no per-turn cap); a 3-step plan grants a 16-iteration budget (PLAN_ITERATIONS_PER_STEP=4), so it burned ~16 model calls before forced finalization (~2-3 min). (B) FRONTEND — Transcript rendered live.elapsed_s, a static server value refreshed only once per loop iteration, so it froze between slow model calls.
- [x] Fix A (plans.py): plan_task gets x-max-successful-calls-per-turn=1 — a second plan_task (re-planning) is blocked ("already succeeded"), so the loop can't burn the budget. Uses Codex's existing cap mechanism. Regression test test_plan_task_capped_to_one_declaration_per_turn (blocks the 2nd call). Note: cap applies whenever plan_task is offered — native tool-calling can only call offered tools, so it always holds when the model actually calls plan_task.
- [x] Fix B (Transcript.jsx v14): elapsed now ticks CLIENT-SIDE (setInterval from stream start), so "working · … · Xs" always counts up regardless of backend pacing. Transpiles OK.
- [x] Offline 214/214 (213 + plan_task cap test). Deploying: restart server (cap) + hard-refresh (timer).
- [x] LIVE-verified on deployed app: timer ticks 14.8s→27.6s (was frozen); "tell me one curious scientific fact" turn completed cleanly (working=false, planTaskMentions=0, no loop) with a real fact + "Hi master" prefix. Server restarted onto the cap; Transcript v14 served.
- [x] Bonus (same directive-classification class): a stray output_suffix='short_joke' would leak the word "short_joke" into replies. Guard added (sensitizer: a joke-sentinel prefix/suffix → conversation_closer) + migration broadened; production cleaned to [output_prefix 'hi master', conversation_closer 'short_joke']. Server restarted.

## Phase 55 — General directive lifecycle (self-growing): follow / change / clear ANY dynamic-content directive
User reframe: jokes/facts are just the TEST — the goal is a system that makes the LLM FOLLOW a directive, CHANGE it (joke→fact), CLEAR it, and LEARN — multilingual, not hardcoded. Rule 1/2/13: the gap is that conversation_opener/closer are content-specific (value hardcoded to "short_joke"), so the slot can only do jokes. Generalize the slot to hold a free-text content_spec; the store/enforce/mirror layers are already content-agnostic (they use `value`).
Investigation done: generate_opener() is joke-hardcoded; router forces value="short_joke"; mirror_directive_nodes projects `value` verbatim (persist/learn = content-agnostic); apply() already supersedes (change) + clears; prefix/suffix already have stop-detection, opener/closer do NOT.
- [x] 1. turn_router: `generate_opener`→`generate_directive_content(content_spec)` + `resilient_opener`→`resilient_content` (produce ONE piece of content matching ANY free-text spec in the spec's own language, never joke-hardcoded). ROUTE_PROMPT/EXTRACT_PROMPT: opener/closer `value` = the CONTENT DESCRIPTION (joke/fact/quote), + a `clear` field for STOP. (hmgfu/turn_router.py:90-115, 19-25, 38-57)
- [x] 2. sensitizer: removed `value="short_joke"` forcing — keeps the router's content_spec (bare sentinel/empty → "a short joke" only as a readable default), passes through `clear`, and generates the fallback via `resilient_content(value)` so it MATCHES the spec (fact→a fact). (hmgfu/sensitizer.py:128-146, 292-302)
- [x] 3. directives: `detect_output_directive` clears opener/closer on an unambiguous cease-cue (`_STOP_STRONG`, excludes "never"/"don't" to avoid qualifier false-positives) and sets a readable spec; `_RENDER` opener/closer now `{value}` + "content itself only, never the instruction text" (leak-safe, general); `_content_spec()` maps the legacy sentinel; `enforce(force_generated)` appends the PERSISTED example (opener always on first_turn; closer only when render suppressed it). Dropped `_DEFAULT_CLOSER_JOKE` + the joke-only "?"/keyword heuristics. (hmgfu/directives.py)
- [x] 4. agent: `enforce(..., force_generated=bool(requested_actions))` mirrors `render_block(suppress_generated=…)` — the closer is force-appended ONLY on action turns (render hid it), ordinary turns trust the prompt (no duplicate). (hmgfu/agent.py:273-277)

### 95.74 — avaliação: o sistema está optimizado para construir apps? (pergunta do utilizador, 16/09)

Levantamento só de leitura, sem alterações. Os carris existem e são bons; a sinalização e o ciclo de
verificação é que não. Evidência de duas execuções reais do mesmo pedido (widget de temporizador).

- [x] **O caminho completo existe**: `write_file` (confinado ao workspace, subpastas, idempotente) →
  widget `app` (`props.file` ou `props.url`) → `GET /workspace-file` (travessia de caminho barrada) →
  iframe com sandbox, botão de recarregar e abrir em separador. Provado vivo no servidor 8777:
  `/workspace-file?path=timer_widget.html` devolve HTTP 200 com 4344 bytes.
- [x] **Rede de segurança**: `auto_serve_built_apps` cria a widget `app` quando o modelo escreve um
  ficheiro web e se esquece dela. Foi isto que salvou as duas execuções, não a intenção do modelo.

  de `create_widget` o descreve bem. Duas fontes de verdade em desacordo. Nas duas execuções o modelo
  inventou um tipo (`timer`, depois `html`) em vez de usar `app`. O prompt até diz "Built web files are
  served to the user automatically", ou seja, anuncia a rede de segurança sem nomear o mecanismo.
- [ ] **DEFEITO 2**: `create_widget` tem tecto de 1 sucesso e 2 falhas por turno. Os palpites de tipo
  errado gastam o orçamento: na segunda execução a terceira chamada foi bloqueada e o modelo ficou sem

- [ ] **DEFEITO 3**: não há ciclo de verificação. Nada abre, executa ou lê erros da página construída

- [ ] **DEFEITO 4**: uma app reconstruída num turno seguinte não se actualiza sozinha — o nonce do
  iframe só muda com o clique manual do utilizador.

### 95.75 — análise da execução de 14:11–14:25 com gemma4:26b (sessão 61915ec3)

Levantamento só de leitura. O modelo executa bem e depressa; o que falha é o contrato do plano.

  t3 chamou `plan_task({"plan": "[x] 0. Research…\n[x] 1. …\n[>] 2. …\n[ ] 3. …"})`. `plans.py:153-158`
  tolera o nome do argumento e o tipo (string → split por linha), mas **não normaliza o texto**: os
  passos ficaram gravados como `"[x] 0. Research current weather data…"`. O estado que o modelo
  declarou ([x], [>]) é descartado e todos os passos nascem pendentes. A partir daí há duas fontes de
  verdade em conflito, e é por isso que nos turnos 7 e 9 o modelo volta a narrar "[X] 0. … [>] 1. …"
  em prosa em vez de usar `update_plan`.
- [x] **P2 — a palavra "widget" no texto do passo exige uma widget de canvas.** `receipts.postcondition`
  (`widget = bool(_WIDGET.search(text)) and not files`): o passo 0 dizia "…design the HTML/JS structure
  for a **weather widget**" e não nomeava ficheiro, por isso o verificador exigiu uma widget chamada
  "weather". O `write_file` de `weather_widget.html` do mesmo turno não conta. Recusa repetida:
  "no receipt touched the widget weather". É esta a falha de ticar o passo.
- [x] **P3 — a rede de segurança cria a widget FORA do sistema de recibos.** `auto_serve_built_apps`
  chama `widget_action` diretamente, depois do `end_turn`, sem recibo. A widget `app`
  `weather_widget.html` existe (w_c5a3f2d6, generated=1, 12:15:36) mas nunca pode satisfazer um passo.
- [x] **P4 — dois passos activos ao mesmo tempo.** A linha final de `session_plans` tem steps[0] e
  steps[1] ambos `active`. `update_plan(step_index=1, status=in_progress)` activa sem desactivar o
  anterior. Invariante a impor: no máximo um passo activo.
- [x] **P5 — um plano PROPOSED substitui o plano activo.** t4 propôs 3 passos com um plano de 4 activo;
  o `update_plan` seguinte respondeu "no active plan — call plan_task first" e os passos antigos
  ficaram órfãos.
- [x] **P6 — sem canal de erros de execução.** Nada capta consola, rede ou `window.onerror` do iframe
  (sem `postMessage`, sem parser, sem headless). O utilizador teve de colar o erro CORS à mão (t6). O

  66 de `weather_widget.html` — e o agente, às cegas, teorizou sobre proxies CORS.

### 95.78 — análise da sessão 523b0720 (13:26–13:31, primeira com as correções a correr)

**O que aguentou.** Nenhum turno perdido, 16 linhas persistidas. O recibo do `write_file` de 3910 bytes
ficou em 3993 chars, **válido, com `_clipped` e as chaves preservadas**, e a sessão lê-se inteira: é a
falha 95.73 provada corrigida em produção. O modelo chamou `create_widget(type="app", props={file})`
**à primeira**, sem inventar tipo (95.74). O plano fechou com prova, coisa que nunca acontecia. O
say-do apanhou a falsa afirmação de criação no t6. O grounding reparou 65°F/63°F no t2 e -0.38 no t8, e
marcou 18°C como não verificado. A directiva de Celsius ficou gravada como `response_style` às 13:27:31.
A pesquisa web funcionou com a chave reposta. O canal de erros não registou nada para a widget nova, e
está certo: a página é estática, nunca falha.

- [x] **D1 — uma oferta em forma de pergunta não regista nada pendente (o pior desta sessão).** No t6
  o modelo perguntou "**Would you like me to rewrite the widget…?**". O say-do só cria proposta a
  partir de uma promessa na primeira pessoa (`c["intent"]`, `saydo.py:383-388`); uma pergunta cai no
  ramo `false_exec_claim` e sai como `corrected_claim`. Resultado: nada pendente. O "yes" do t7 e o
  "yes" do t8 foram descartados, o `plan_task` foi recusado **três vezes** com "nothing is pending to
  confirm or refuse -- ask the user what they want done", que é exactamente o conselho errado: o
  utilizador já tinha sido perguntado e já tinha respondido. Dois turnos gastos a pedir o mesmo.
- [x] **D2 — o passo do plano é uma frase da prosa do modelo, e expulsou o plano verdadeiro.** No t4 a
  oferta virou plano de um passo cujo texto é `saydo.py:383` a limpar o "I'll" da frase: "Since this
  requires fetching live data and designing the interface, I'll need to write the HTML/JavaScript code
  and then". No t5 o modelo declarou o plano real de 2 passos e foi recusado com `already_active`;
  depois `update_plan(step=1)` deu "step must be 0..0".
- [x] **D3 — um recibo de leitura fechou o passo.** O passo em prosa não nomeia ficheiro, widget nem
  ferramenta, por isso caiu no ramo genérico e o `bash cat maputo_weather_widget.html` do t6 casou por
  sobreposição de palavras ("html"). O recibo declara `effect: read` e o ramo genérico ignora essa
  coluna. Evidência: `d65e83551f83` é o `bash`, com `consumed_by=0`.
- [x] **D4 — nada liga a widget no canvas ao ficheiro que o agente inspecciona.** Construiu

  Setembro), explicando ao utilizador um ficheiro que não é a widget: disse "static template showing
  28°C" quando o que escreveu tem 18.

  `temp: 18, // Converting 64F to approx 18C`, com um comentário na 99 a dizer que "in production"
  usaria uma API com chave. O 18 vem do 64°F que a pesquisa devolveu no t2. O utilizador via 33 no
  telemóvel. Escrever o ficheiro é trabalho real, por isso o say-do não tem nada a apanhar: falta uma
  verificação de que um artefacto que promete dados ao vivo os vá de facto buscar.

### 95.78 — os cinco corrigidos de forma geral, cada um no contrato que os origina

- [x] **D1 (offers.py, speech_act.offers_to_act)**: a oferta deixa de depender da gramática. Uma
  resposta que TERMINA a perguntar se o assistente deve fazer algo fica pendente, tal como uma promessa
  na primeira pessoa. O predicado compõe-se dos que já existiam — `is_interrogative`,
  `requests_side_effect` — mais pessoa gramatical; não inventa vocabulário. O registo acontece num só
  sítio, o invólucro de `enforce`, e é ortogonal à decisão sobre as afirmações: a correção do t6
  continua a sair, e a oferta fica na mesma pendente.
- [x] **D2 (offers.is_placeholder / adopt_declared_steps)**: um plano que a harness sintetizou de prosa
  é um PLACEHOLDER. Quando o modelo declara os passos reais para o mesmo pedido aprovado, eles
  substituem-no e a aprovação que o placeholder ganhou mantém-se. O guarda 67.11 continua a valer para
  planos declarados pelo modelo: só o placeholder cede.
- [x] **D3 (speech_act.changes_the_world + receipts)**: no ramo genérico, um recibo cujo efeito
  declarado é `read` nunca fecha um passo que pede uma mudança. Lê-se a coluna `effect`, que vem do
  schema da ferramenta, em vez de adivinhar pelo texto do resultado. Os verbos são a metade
  TRANSFORMADORA do inventário que `_ACTION_OPENER` já tinha; a metade de leitura ficou de fora, por
  isso "list the files" e "check my memory" continuam a ser provados por leituras.
- [x] **D4 (operational_state + app_errors.session_app_files)**: o bloco de estado passa a dizer que
  ficheiro cada app do canvas mostra. Reutiliza a função que o canal de erros já tinha, sem duplicar.
- [x] **D5 (artefacts.py)**: o que foi escrito é lido no momento em que é escrito, os marcadores de
  rascunho ficam no recibo, e a harness anexa a divulgação à resposta. **Compromisso declarado**: os
  marcadores são uma lista curta de idiomas de código (TODO, mock, YOUR_API_KEY, "in production"…),
  visível no módulo e aqui, com correspondência por palavra inteira para não apanhar prosa comum. A
  alternativa completa — executar o artefacto para ver se faz o que diz — é uma mudança muito maior.
- [x] **Tectos respeitados**: `saydo.py` estava exactamente em 400, por isso o sufixo da proposta (o
  que o utilizador LÊ quando lhe oferecem trabalho) mudou-se para `offers.py`, com os dois nomes
  reexportados em `saydo` para nenhum chamador ou teste partir (Regra 11). Guarda de arquitectura verde.
- [x] **Provas**: `v278` (7 casos, incluindo a troca completa pelo motor real: oferta em pergunta, um
  único "yes", plano adoptado, zero recusas), `v279` (5), `v280` (4), `v281` (5). Suite completa
  **2200 passed, 1 xfailed**.
- [x] **A correr**: servidor 8777 reiniciado às 13:49 UTC (parado há 18 min, nenhum turno a decorrer),
  com o 95.77 e o 95.78. Health passa a anunciar `chat: gemma4:26b`, que é o que o turno usa. Verificado

  `weather_widget_final.html`; e esse ficheiro acusa cinco marcadores — placeholder, "In production
  you'd", YOUR_API_KEY, Mocking, mockData.

### 95.79 — as três últimas conversas, e a causa única por trás dos dois erros

Sessões `d7f69149` (14:09), `87e75027` (14:15–14:21) e `6c01c259` (14:22), com `chat_model=gemma4:26b`
e `thinking_mode="always"`.

**A memória fez o seu trabalho.** O `memory_search` do t2 encontrou "i use to have a plant named fern
and i gave it to Bruna"; no t3 a correção para Ingrid foi aceite e o sistema registou a contradição
com a mais recente a ganhar. Nada disto falhou.

- [ ] **E1 — o canal de raciocínio derramado.** Resposta gravada, literal:
  `"thought\n<channel|>It sounds like you're missing Fern! ..."`. A resposta CERTA vem a seguir ao
  marcador. O depurador de tokens especiais (`thinking._SPECIAL_RE`) só apanha `<|...|>`, com barra
  vertical dos DOIS lados; `<channel|>` só a tem de um, e a palavra solta `thought` na linha anterior
  não é apanhada por nada. Terceira ocorrência registada na base (523b0720 t7, 6daa1883 t3).
- [ ] **E2 — "empty chat response (ollama degraded)" é um diagnóstico errado.** Provado, não inferido:
  reprodução com o prompt real, 22 chamadas, **9 com conteúdo vazio, todas com `think=True`**, todas
  com `done_reason: stop`, 226 a 673 tokens gerados e o bloco `thinking` cheio (800 a 2700 chars).
  **Todas as chamadas com `think=False` devolveram conteúdo.** No log do Ollama, as três tentativas
  falhadas do utilizador foram HTTP 200 com 379 a 587 tokens decodificados. Ou seja: o modelo GERA,
  mas termina depois do canal de análise sem emitir o canal final. O `providers.py` lê só
  `message.content`, ignora `message.thinking` que acabou de receber, chama-lhe degradação do Ollama e
  repete três vezes a mesma coisa, gastando ~15 s antes de matar o turno.
- [x] **Não é falta de memória da GPU** (a minha primeira suspeita, descartada com dados): a 3090 está
  a 23781/24576 MiB com três modelos residentes e o 26b com contexto 262144, mas o Ollama respondeu
  200 em todas as tentativas e o modelo decodificou centenas de tokens. Pressão de memória há; causa
  deste erro, não é.
- [x] **O sistema já conhecia este fenómeno noutro modelo**: `thinking.resolve_think` força
  `think=False` nos turnos de acção porque "native reasoning BURIES the tool call and the model stops
  early (ornith/Qwen3.5)". O 26b passou a fazê-lo também em turnos normais, onde o `think` continua a
  True porque a definição está em `always`.
- [ ] **E3 — o valor proposto é a frase inteira.** d7f69149: "Should I record that plant named Fern is
  **i use to have a plant named fern and i gave it to Bruna**?" O slot do valor levou a mensagem toda.
- [ ] **E4 — clarificação sobre nada.** 87e75027 t3: "I could not check '' against what you wrote --
  could you say it again in full?", com o rótulo vazio entre aspas.

**Contorno imediato, sem código**: `thinking_mode` de `always` para `off` nas Definições. Na
reprodução, todas as chamadas com `think=False` devolveram resposta. `dynamic` NÃO resolve: omite o
parâmetro e o gemma pensa por omissão.

### 95.81 — o telemóvel: a casca media-se mais fern do que o ecrã

- [x] **Causa, uma linha** (`web/index.html`): `#root { height: 100vh; width: 100vw; }`. Num telemóvel
  `100vh` conta a barra de endereço e a barra inferior retrácteis, tipicamente 60 a 120 px a mais do
  que se vê. Tudo o que a casca dimensiona a partir da sua própria altura herda o erro: o painel de
  Definições tem `max-height: 88%` **dessa** caixa, por isso o fundo dele e a barra de escrever ficam
  debaixo do próprio cromado do browser. É exactamente o que o utilizador descreveu.
- [x] **Correcção**: `#root` passa a `100dvh` — a altura que está mesmo no ecrã — com a regra `100vh`
  a ficar primeiro como recurso para browsers sem `dvh`; a largura vem do pai em vez de `100vw`, que
  conta a barra de deslocamento; o `<meta viewport>` ganha `viewport-fit=cover`; e a barra de escrever
  (`Transcript.jsx`) soma `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` ao seu espaçamento, para o botão Enviar não
  ficar por baixo do indicador do telemóvel. O cache-buster do Transcript foi incrementado.
- [x] **Teste**: `v282`, cinco casos a falhar primeiro, incluindo o de o ficheiro alterado ter de ser
  mesmo re-obtido pelo browser. Suite completa **2206 passed, 1 xfailed**.
- [x] **Medido no browser a 375x640**: casca 640 px, sem transbordo, painel de Definições de 38 a 602
  dentro do ecrã e rolável, com 3283 px de conteúdo alcançável.
- [ ] **Por confirmar no telemóvel real**: o emulador não tem barra retráctil, por isso `vh` e `dvh`
  valem o mesmo lá dentro e o mecanismo não se reproduz. A prova final é o teu telefone.
- [ ] **Se persistir com o teclado aberto**: o passo seguinte é reagir ao `visualViewport`, que é o que
  muda quando o teclado sobe. Fica identificado, não feito.
